l.i: Beza, tibi tanto pro munere reddam?
Qui luctu tabentem atro, penitúsque arentem
Erexti, mentémque sua mihi sede reponis?
At dignum te, Beza, nihil, nisi vota piorum:
Nec vero prodesse neges tibi vota piorum.
Ecce etiam Iani poscunt sua vota Calenda.
Esto igitur felix nascentis circulus anni
Beza tibi, atque aliæ felices ordine centum,
Et, quæ Cæsareis solennia vota triumphis,
Incolumes tibi de nostris Deus augeat annos:
Quis nescit quonis [?] potiorem Cæsare Bezam?

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "quonis" in the last line of the first block is read as printed but uncertain. The first-block line-ends are read from the scan. The verse is printed in italic throughout, and the initial L of "Lectium" is a large capital. The poem's last word "Turbidos" stands at the page foot and continues on the next page. Headings set in small capitals are transcribed in plain capitals.
